The Prophet tells Hakim bin Hizam that wealth taken without greed is blessed and the giving hand better, so Hakim never asks again, refusing even his booty share.
May the slave of dinar, dirham and fine clothes, pleased only when given, perish, while Paradise is for the dusty fighter holding his horse's reins, content at front or rear.
Some people spend Allah's wealth unjustly, and they will be put in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
The Prophet tells Hakim that wealth taken without greed is blessed and the giving hand is better, so Hakim never again accepts anything, even from Abu Bakr and Umar.
Perish the slave of money and clothes; man would want a third valley of gold; true wealth is a content soul; the rich have little reward unless they give.
In the shade of the Ka'bah the Prophet kept swearing that the wealthy are the losers, except those who spend their wealth this way and that.
Umar urged a man refusing pay for public work to take it, as the Prophet bade Umar take unsought money, keep it, then give it in charity, never seeking it.
